messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty page fired (INC-2026-1301) — embeddings-eu high tail latency. Trigger: embeddings-queue > 95th pct for 3m. Affected route: /v1/embeddings (eu). Severity: sev2. PD link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-2026-1301

sam: grabbing this — on-call. joining bridge now.

pagerbot: auto-ack by sam (on-call). escalation hold 6m.

leah: noted. any customer-facing impact yet? can help draft a note.

sam: initial triage: eu dedicated pool showing sustained queuing, workers healthy but KV-cache churn high. about ~3% of embeddings requests hitting >10s, some 500s. not full outage but elevated latencies.

omar: is this the same pattern as yesterday's kvcache spike?

sam: looks similar but different root — yesterday was a model rollout; no rollout here. suspect a hot-prefix surge (long sequences) causing large KV footprint & eviction.

leah: ok. i'll prep status page blurb: "We're seeing increased embedding latencies in EU. Engineers are investigating; operations in progress." want me to post?

sam: yes please post as "Investigating" and add PD link.

oncall-sre: actionable items i can take: 1) bump autoscale burst for eu-embed pool 2) flip routing fallback to us for non-legal customers 3) increase kvcache size on the most impacted hosts (rolling). want me to run 1 and 2 now?

sam: go ahead with 1) and 2). before 3) i'll patch config on a single host to validate.

oncall-sre: running: `infractl autoscale set --pool eu-embed --burst 2x && infractl route toggle --from eu --to us --predicate "!legal_customer"`

pagerbot: routing toggle executed by oncall-sre. autoscale change queued to rollout.

sam: small snippet from logs around 1805554300:
```
2026-04-02T18:45:01Z embeddings-queue: worker-7 latency=12912ms kv_evictions=412 prefix_hits=11
2026-04-02T18:45:02Z embeddings-queue: worker-3 latency=15321ms kv_evictions=690 prefix_hits=2
```

omar: oof. those eviction rates are huge. does increasing cache size reduce throughput? any memory pressure?

oncall-sre: memory headroom ok on most hosts; increasing kvcache size on one host now for test. will monitor.

leah: posted status page note (Investigating). link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/INC-2026-1301

sam: customer impact summary for postmortem: "Embeddings requests in EU experienced elevated latency (median ~500ms, 95th up to 15s) and small fraction of 5xx for ~10 minutes while autoscaling and fallback completed. Non-legal customers were temporarily routed to US fallback to mitigate."

oncall-sre: rolling kvcache bump applied to one host — initial latency drop observed on that host (95th down ~40%). applying to remainder.

pagerbot: page severity reduced to sev3 (manual). acknowledging continued monitoring.

sam: great. i'll keep pings every 2m. next update in 2m.

leah: drafted customer note for affected tenants; waiting on final numbers before send.

sam: update: autoscale finished, routing fallback absorbed ~18% of eu traffic, overall 95th dropped to ~1.2s. will keep monitoring for 15 more mins.

omar: can we capture a short runbook step so we don't page repeatedly for same symptom? maybe a kvcache auto-bump when eviction rate > 200/min?

sam: agree — adding a follow-up action for runbook.

leah: sending customer notifications now with interim mitigation summary.

oncall-sre: monitoring green for 10m; no new 5xx spikes.

sam: thanks team. marking as mitigated but leaving incident open for postmortem tasks. will post timeline & RCA later.

pagerbot: incident marked mitigated by sam. follow-ups: runbook update, kvcache auto-bump alert, postmortem assigned to sam + leah + oncall-sre.

leah: adding postmortem template now.

sam: closing bridge in 1m. final customer note updated. thanks all :white_check_mark:

oncall-sre: nice work.

pagerbot: closing page thread — monitor window 30m.

sam: thread closed.
